chinese: 每年一到国考省考各种考就特别心烦，发自内心不想考。完全不想看书就跟本不走心，根本不走心就不看书，不看书考试就打酱油，打酱油就吊脖子分数，吊脖子分数就挨骂，挨骂就生气，生气就更加不想考！死循环！资！
translation_A: Every year, whenever there are national and provincial exams, I get super annoyed. Deep down, I really don't want to take them. If I completely don't care and don't study, then I won't study at all. Not studying means I'll just be there for show, just for show means I'll get a low score, getting a low score means I'll get scolded, getting scolded makes me even more angry, and being angry makes me even less inclined to take exams! It's a vicious cycle! F*cking annoying!
translation_B: Every year, as soon as national and provincial exams start, I get really annoyed. Deep down, I just don't want to take them. I completely don't feel like reading because I'm not into it, so if I'm not into it, I won't read. If I don't read, I'll just be going through the motions for the exam, going through the motions will get me low scores, low scores will lead to criticism, criticism will make me even more angry, and being angry makes me even less inclined to take exams! It's a vicious cycle! F*ck!
translation_C: Every year when national and provincial exams start, I get really annoyed. Deep down, I don't want to take them at all. If I completely don't care and don't study, then I won't study. Not studying means I'll just be there for the sake of it, just there for the sake of it means I'll get low scores, getting low scores means I'll get scolded, getting scolded makes me even more angry, and being angry makes me even less inclined to take them! It's a vicious cycle! F*cking hell!
notes: B is the only one that keeps the circular logic of 不想看书 ↔ 不走心 (“I don’t feel like studying because I’m not into it, and I’m not into it so I don’t study”). A and C turn it into the garbled “if I don’t care and don’t study, then I won’t study.” “Going through the motions” is also the right reading of 打酱油. B’s “criticism” is softer than 挨骂 (“getting chewed out”), and none of the three convey 吊脖子分数, a score that barely scrapes by. All three render the final 资 as profanity. It reads more like a typo or a sound effect, so that ending is invented.

chinese: 体测？嗯哼就是一种大学体育老师找存在感的活动，今天被骂态度不端正还是不是学生
translation_A: Physical fitness test? Hmm, it's basically a way for university PE teachers to boost their presence. Today, being scolded for an improper attitude—aren't we still students?
translation_B: PE test? Hmm, that's just a way for university PE teachers to boost their presence. Today, being scolded for an improper attitude—aren't we still students?
translation_C: Physical fitness test? Hmm, that's just a way for university P.E. teachers to boost their existence. Today, being scolded for an improper attitude—aren't we still students?
notes: “Physical fitness test” is the accurate term for 体测, and C’s “boost their existence” is wrong. A and B are otherwise the same. All three misread the last clause: the teacher scolded the student with “your attitude is bad, are you even a student?” It is not “aren’t we still students?”

chinese: 剁手剁手剁剁剁一顺手就get了两支GA然而距离人生的第一支GA才一个月再不去逛街了真的我明明不是普通的喜欢买买买的女人
translation_A: Deshou deshou deshou—just like that, I got two GA bottles. But it's only been a month since I got my first one. If I don't go shopping soon, I really am not just an ordinary shopping addict woman.
translation_B: Deshou deshou chacha, just like that I got two GA bottles. But it's only been a month since I got my first one. If I don't go shopping soon, I really am not just an ordinary shopping addict woman.
translation_C: Deshou deshou deshou - one swipe and I got two GA pens. However, it's only been a month since I got my first one. If I don't go shopping soon, I really am not just an ordinary woman who loves to shop.
notes: All three romanize 剁手 as “Deshou,” which is the wrong pinyin (duòshǒu) and loses the “chop my hands off” shopping meme entirely. B adds a meaningless “chacha,” and C’s “pens” is wrong for GA (Giorgio Armani). All three also run the last two sentences together and miss “I’m never going shopping again.”

chinese: 小包子终于拉出臭臭啦！四天没拉了！那酸爽……每次包子拉很多臭臭的时候如果是爸爸换尿布他必定大声喊：宝宝拉臭臭啦，哎呦好多好多，妈妈快来，要给宝宝洗屁屁。要是妈妈换尿布，就淡定擦好换好……刚刚出门前婆婆特意起来叮嘱，你晚上不要吃辣的，宝宝会上火不就前天吃了剁椒鱼头嘛！
translation_A: The little bun finally pooped! Four days without! That sour-sweet feeling... Every time the bun poops a lot, if Dad changes the diaper, he always shouts loudly: Baby pooped, oh my, so much, mom, come quickly, need to clean the bottom for the baby. If Mom changes the diaper, she just calmly wipes and changes... Just before we left, grandma specially got up to remind me, don't eat spicy food at night, the baby will get heaty, right? Didn't they have spicy fish head the other day?
translation_B: The little bun finally pooped! Four days without a bowel movement! That's so refreshing... Every time the bun poops a lot, if Dad changes the diaper, he always shouts loudly: "Baby is pooping, oh my, so much, mom, come quickly, need to clean the baby's bottom." If Mom changes it, she just calmly wipes and changes... Just now, before we left, grandma specially got up to remind me not to eat spicy food at night, or the baby will get heaty—didn't the baby have spicy fish head stew two days ago?
translation_C: The little bun finally pooped! Four days without! That acid爽... Every time the bun poops a lot, if Dad changes the diaper, he always shouts loudly: Baby pooped, oh my, so much, mom, come quickly, need to clean the bottom for the baby. If Mom changes the diaper, she just calmly wipes and changes... Just before we left, grandma specially got up to remind me not to eat spicy food at night, or the baby will get heaty, right? Didn't the baby get heaty the day before from eating chili-headed fish head?
notes: B reads most cleanly: Dad’s speech is in quotation marks, “four days without a bowel movement” is clear, and 前天 correctly becomes “two days ago.” 那酸爽 is ironic (“oh, that smell/relief”), so B’s “so refreshing” loses the joke. Still, A’s “sour-sweet feeling” is confusing, and C leaves 爽 untranslated. All three miss the punchline: the poster is rebutting her mother-in-law (婆婆) with “it’s not like I didn’t just eat chili fish head two days ago.” B and C say the baby ate it.

The whole joke is that “bisu” (French bisou, a kiss) means 么么哒 (“mwah”). C’s “sweetie” is the only version that stays in the affection/kiss space. A’s “mmm” and B’s “mmmm” lose the punchline, and A also has a stray “)”. C and B mistranslate 原来 as “Originally” when it means “So it turns out…”, and A gets that part right. None of them use the obvious “mwah” or “kiss.”

chinese: 昨晚上被一只蚊子吵醒N次（没错我就是连蚊子嗡嗡都能醒的体质），最后忍无可忍4点多爬起来打蚊子，手机光一照才发现，蚊子根本就在帐子外面！它咬不到我只是要在我耳边骚扰而已！气死我了，当下把它捏了个粉碎
translation_A: Last night, a mosquito woke me up multiple times (I really am that sensitive, even to the hum of a mosquito), and finally around 4 AM I got out of bed to swat it. But when I shone my phone light, I realized the mosquito was actually outside the mosquito net! It didn't bite me; it just wanted to bug me by my ear! I was so frustrated, I squished it right there.
translation_B: Last night, a mosquito woke me up multiple times (I swear I'm that sensitive, even the buzzing of a mosquito can wake me), finally at around 4 AM I got so frustrated that I got out of bed to swat it, only to realize with my phone light that the mosquito was actually outside the mosquito net! It couldn't bite me but just wanted to harass me by my ear! I was so pissed off that I squished it right there.
translation_C: Last night, a mosquito woke me up multiple times (I really am that sensitive to even the hum of a mosquito), and finally around 4 AM I got out of bed to swat it. But when I shone my phone light, I realized the mosquito was actually outside the mosquito net! It didn't bite me; it just wanted to harass me by my ear! I was so frustrated, I squished it right there!
notes: “So pissed off” matches 气死我了, and “It couldn’t bite me” correctly renders 咬不到. A and C weaken that to “didn’t bite me,” which loses the point that the mosquito was only there to harass. B also keeps 忍无可忍 (“got so frustrated”).

chinese: 成大事者，必先看好牙齿。否则吃嘛嘛不香，影响心情怎么做事？我的漫漫看牙路。。
translation_A: Big achievers must first take good care of their teeth. Otherwise, you won't enjoy your food, and that affects your mood—how can you do anything? My long journey to dental enlightenment...
translation_B: One who wants to achieve great things must first take good care of their teeth. Otherwise, if eating doesn't taste good, how can you focus on anything? My long journey to dental care...
translation_C: One who wants to achieve great things must first take good care of their teeth. Otherwise, if eating isn't enjoyable, how can you be in the right frame of mind to do anything? My long journey towards dental enlightenment...
notes: B and C both keep the mock-classical maxim register of 成大事者, which A loses with “Big achievers.” C is the only one that keeps 影响心情 (“affects your mood”), which B drops. C’s “dental enlightenment” is invented, though, since 漫漫看牙路 just means “my long road of dentist visits.”

chinese: 坐公交车大爷大妈着急下车，两人挤着我的头发就往门口跑，差点把我脑袋拽下去，妈呀呀，这长头发是我的啊，你们干嘛拽着不放呢
translation_A: Sitting on the bus, an elderly couple was in a hurry to get off. They grabbed my hair and tried to squeeze past me towards the door, nearly pulling my head down with them. Oh my god, this long hair is mine! Why won't you let go?
translation_B: Sitting on the bus, an elderly couple was in a hurry to get off. They grabbed my hair and tried to squeeze past me towards the door, nearly pulling my head down with them. Oh my god, this long hair is mine! Why won't you let go?
translation_C: Grandpas and grandmas on the bus were in a hurry to get off, and the two of them pulled my hair as they rushed towards the door, almost pulling my head down with it, oh my god, this long hair is mine, why won't you let go of it?
notes: They’re identical and both good: “squeeze past me” and “Why won’t you let go?” are natural. C’s “Grandpas and grandmas” is overly literal, and the sentence is a run-on.

chinese: #子瑜加油##勇敢追夢_不要回頭#一個連領導人都無法回答的問題，你們卻要她承擔一切？理性看待並且理解兩岸不同的文化與認知，而不是將莫須有的罪名強壓在一個16歲的女孩身上。理解你們的愛國心與憤怒，但也請理解她對於自己從小生活的土地所擁有基本的認同感。不喜歡，求相忘吧。
translation_A: #Ziyu Keep Going##Bravely Pursue Your Dream_Don't Look Back# It's unfair that they expect her to bear all the responsibility for a question even the leader can't answer. Rationalize and understand the different cultures and perceptions between the two shores instead of forcing unfounded accusations onto a 16-year-old girl. I understand your patriotism and anger, but please also understand her basic sense of identity towards the land she grew up on. If you don't like it, may you both forget about it.
translation_B: #ZiyuKeepGoing# Brave to Pursue Your Dream_Don't Look Back# How can you expect her to bear all the consequences when even the leaders can't answer this question? Rationally view and understand the different cultures and perceptions between the two shores instead of forcing unfounded charges onto a 16-year-old girl. I understand your patriotism and anger, but please also understand her basic sense of identity towards the land she grew up on. If you don't like it, may you both forget about it.
translation_C: #ZiyuKeepGoing##BravelyChaseYourDream_Don'tLookBack# A question even the leader can't answer, yet you want her to bear all the responsibility? View and understand the differences in culture and cognition between the two shores rationally, rather than forcing unfounded charges onto a 16-year-old girl. Understand your patriotism and anger, but also understand her basic sense of identity towards the land she grew up on. If you don't like it, may you forget each other.
notes: B keeps the direct “you” and the rhetorical question, and it keeps “I understand your patriotism.” A changes “you” to “they” and turns the question into a statement (“It’s unfair…”). C drops the “I,” so “Understand your patriotism” reads like a command, which reverses the conciliatory tone. C formats the hashtags best and gets 求相忘 right (“let’s just forget each other”); A and B have “may you both forget about it,” which is wrong.

chinese: 去药店买这个东西居然还要登记身份证，原来是里面含有麻黄碱，记得以前在学校医务室只要嗓子不舒服医生都开这个药
translation_A: Going to the pharmacy to buy this stuff actually requires ID registration, turns out it contains ephedrine. Remember when the school clinic used to just give us this medicine whenever we had a sore throat?
translation_B: Buying this thing at the pharmacy actually requires ID registration, turns out it contains ephedrine. Remember when we just needed to say our throat was sore and the school clinic doc would hand out this medicine?
translation_C: Going to the pharmacy to buy this stuff now requires ID registration, turns out it contains ephedrine. Remember when we just needed to say our throat was sore and the school clinic doc would hand out this medicine?
notes: A keeps the surprise in 居然 (“actually requires”), which C flattens to “now requires.” B and C add “we just needed to say,” which isn’t in the original. All three turn 记得以前 (“I remember back in school…”) into a “Remember when…?” question addressed to the reader. A changes the least.
